title: Copying a value of nested aliases to a place before their anchors must not write the expansion out unbounded
notes: The destination, the first member, comes before every anchor. An alias must not come before its anchor, so the copy cannot keep the aliases it holds: the family rule is that an alias whose anchor would not precede it is written out as the value it stands for. Here the value copied is ten levels of ten aliases, so writing it out makes ten billion scalars from an input of under five hundred bytes, as in a billion-laughs document. The bytes a patch copies, aliases written out included, are charged to the alias-expansion byte budget, so a conforming library fails with a limit error and leaves the document unchanged. A library that writes them out without a bound fails on memory or time, and one that keeps the aliases in front of their anchors writes a document that does not read back.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that copied a value of nested aliases to a place before their anchors and wrote the aliases out as the expansion with no bound, so a small input grew without limit.
